en.html:
An unexpectedly good breakfast, finished. The sisters had been sent home. I was taking one quiet breath over the tea they had left when Muramasa, out on patrol, contacted me through the metal-echo.

One breath only. Apparently I had become greedy. Food, tea, and now air also without interruption? Bhai, leave something for the next man. At this rate I would be expecting to finish the cup while it still contained warmth.

The morning had corrected this dangerous tendency immediately.

I acknowledged Yagenta with my eyes and stood. That much seemed enough for him to understand. A silent nod came back.

Very good. Neither of us had said anything, and yet the conversation was complete. With other people I could explain myself at considerable length and leave them more disturbed than before. Here I had contributed nothing and been understood at once.

Perhaps the contribution was the difficulty. No time to investigate it now.

The contest over distance had reached deadlock. My side, however, held the advantage.

And yet, mixed with the mountain's noise... that idling sound...

Kitni mehnat karta hai. How thoroughly the fellow worked. Tongue also had first-class sword training.

His analysis was exact. Start an armoured air battle here, and precisely that outcome became likely.

Still he did not armour up and flee. Why? Because I might choose stupidity. Defeat him separately, kill him, return afterward—as though the rest of the world would wait while I completed my preferred order of business. He had allowed for my idiocy also. Most considerate.

Day before yesterday, one glimpse only, but his tsurugi seemed a military mass-production model. Speed mein, no assurance he could escape us.

Catch him, bring him down, that I trusted I could do. Leave the mountain undefended, that risk I could not take. Armoured combat had practically been closed from my side.

Zubaan se hi. Tongue alone, and he had locked away my decisive strength. No celebration on his face, no carelessness in the next movement. Cautious only. This experience belonged to another order of man.
